newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan files to have U.S. ship sanctions withdrawn.
newsitem.headline: Japan files to have U.S. ship sanctions withdrawn.

text.p: Three leading Japanese shipping companies have asked a U.S. court to repeal a U.S. government decision to impose retaliatory surcharges on Japanese vessels because of a port dispute, a Japanese shipping body said on Monday.

Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK together presented a petition of review to a U.S. appeals court in Washington on March 28, a Japanese Ship Owners' Association spokesman said.
The three shipping companies are asking that the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission's (FMC) decision to impose retaliatory surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports be nullified.

The commission has said that $100,000 port surcharges on Japanese vessels will be imposed in retaliation for what it calls "unfavourable restrictive practices" at Japanese ports. The punitive measure will take effect on April 14.
The Japanese firms say that the commission's decision is unfair.

Last month, Japanese Ship Owners' Association Chairman Isao Shintani said in a statement that "the U.S. decision is highly improper, not only because there is a strong possibility that the measures could violate a U.S.-Japan treaty on commerce and navigation, but also because the sanctions...are directed at three innocent Japanese shipping firms."
